item.title: Melania Trump calls for lasting Ukraine truce as she hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials
item.description:
As war rages on in Kyiv and other cities, the first lady celebrates her single-city ceasefire with Russian and Ukrainian envoys Beaming from a podium in the White House’s Grand Foyer, Melania Trump welcomed senior Russian and Ukrainian officials on Thursday to celebrate a ceasefire in an embattled Ukrainian town for which she has become the unlikeliest broker. The evacuation from Oleshky, a frontline Ukrainian town now occupied by Russia where 800 people lived through a protracted humanitarian crisis, may seem like a sideshow at this point in the war. Russian missiles and drones continue to rain down on Kyiv and other major cities, and a single Russian strike described as a “double-tap” bombing killed 40 people in Zaporizhzhia on Wednesday. item.title: Paraguay’s president quits after millions of people’s savings frozen in bank crisis
item.description:
Santiago Peña’s rightwing administration had authorised Ueno Bank to drastically expand operations before collapse Paraguay’s rightwing president, Santiago Peña, resigned on Thursday after a political and financial crisis collapsed the South American country’s banking system in recent days. At the centre of the crisis is Ueno Bank, which in just a few years under Peña went from an obscure digital bank to one of the country’s largest lenders, claiming to have about 60% of Paraguay’s adult population as customers. item.title: We’ve just seen a transformative moment in America’s death penalty history | Austin Sarat
item.description:
In summary If approved by the California Supreme Court, the number of people sentenced to death nationwide would drop by nearly a third. California Gov. Gavin Newsom today moved to commute the death sentences of all 548 people facing execution in the state, allowing them to instead serve life sentences without the possibility of parole. The California Supreme Court must approve some of these commutations. If it does, Newsom’s action would be responsible for the largest mass commutation of death sentences in U.S. history . “I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” he wrote in an open letter to Californians . Newsom’s decision, which his office said would benefit 529 men and 19 women, does not guarantee they will all be resentenced. The justices will have to decide…

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed did not have to become less Muslim to win
item.description:
Progressive Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan’s U.S. Senate race was one of the most-watched contests in the 2026 midterm elections. As the results for this race came in, I had my eye on one demographic: Black voters. I am a political scientist who studies Black political behavior. My research has been published in numerous journals , as well as in my forthcoming book, “Black Resilience,” which examines Black voters’ political participation. Wayne County voters The support of Black voters for El-Sayed was not a given. In the August primary, 62% of Detroit voters chose U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens over El-Sayed. Many pundits predicted it would be difficult for El-Sayed to gain support in Detroit, which is about 75% Black . item.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
item.description:
Wong, 30, in prison since 2020, is only activist in Hong Kong prosecuted twice under national security law Exclusive: Joshua Wong laments city’s fate from inside maximum security prison The Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after earlier pleading guilty to “foreign collusion”, his second conviction under a national security law critics say has been used to silence political opposition in the city. Wong, who rose to prominence as the teenage face of Hong Kong’s 2014 pro-democracy demonstrations, submitted his guilty plea in September. He had been accused of working with the exiled Hong Kong activist Nathan Law to urge foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures against China. Continue reading...

item.title: After taking control of Congress, Democrats vow major probes into Trump's 'tentacles of corruption'
item.description:
Left: Kansas Democratic Senate candidate Adam Hamilton. Right: Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Photos by Jim Vondruska/Getty Images; Alex Wong/Getty Images. Democrats have taken full control of the U.S. Congress in a massive repudiation of Donald Trump’s authoritarian presidency and his gross mishandling of the economy. The blue wave that observers have projected for months ended up being a blue tsunami Tuesday night. Democrats are expected to win a significant majority in the House of Representatives, and they’ve already flipped seven Senate seats held by Republicans. For the first two years of Trump’s second term, Republicans have held a governing trifecta, denying Democrats much opportunity to block their agenda or hold the president and his corrupt administration accountable. item.title: US Justice Department sues Penn State over undocumented students’ tuition
item.description:
The Trump administration is suing Pennsylvania State University over a policy that allegedly allows undocumented migrant students to qualify for in-state tuition. In a lawsuit filed on Thursday, the Justice Department argued that in-state tuition for undocumented migrants discriminates against U.S. citizens because U.S. citizens living outside Pennsylvania are not eligible for the same reduced tuition rate. "Congress made a deliberate policy choice that states and their public institutions may not grant tuition benefits to illegal aliens unless those same benefits are made to all U.S. citizens," Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the DOJ's Civil Division said in a statement. "This university has ignored that mandate. The Department will continue to challenge policies that unlawfully disadvantage American citizens," he continued. JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SUES COLORADO OVER IN-STATE…

item.title: Anti-Trans Panic Couldn’t Save Republicans in Deep-Red Texas
item.description:
On an election night handing Republicans a beating in critical House and Senate races across the country, the GOP fell short even in once deep-red Texas after a campaign run on a go-to outrage tactic: fearmongering over the rights of transgender people. Democrats escaped the political wilderness in the Longhorn State on Tuesday night, when Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton — despite the far-right attorney general’s relentless attacks on the trans community and his party’s claims that Democrats would enforce so-called “transgenderism” as a kind of ideology. item.title: Israel president to announce Sunday who will form new government
item.description:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday, November 8, whom he will task with trying to form a new government, following post-election talks with all party leaders. 46 parliament members recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, while 67 backed his opponent Gadi Eisenkot. Seven lawmakers abstained.
